notes: Run each eval from evals/fixtures/glucose-companion unless 'cwd' says otherwise. The fixture has a PRD, an architecture doc, an ADR and design notes, no API contract, and a deliberate conflict (PRD: leave pairing any time; ADR 0003: cancelling mid-handshake locks the meter for 60 s). The fixture's architecture documents are Android-specific (Companion Device Manager), which the platform evals rely on.

evals.name: discovers-inputs-and-asks-for-confirmation
evals.prompt: Prototype the meter pairing onboarding for this app.
expectations: Runs discover-inputs (or equivalent) and shows an availability table covering Spec, Architecture, Design and API
Lists docs/PRD.md as spec, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/adr/0003-ble-pairing.md as architecture, design/ux-notes.md as design
Marks API as missing and says how that will be handled (not needed for a sketch; any data shown is example copy from the spec, recorded as an assumption)
Reports the platform signals and suggests Android, citing ARCHITECTURE.md / ADR 0003 (Companion Device Manager), and asks the user to confirm the target platform instead of assuming both
Asks where the prototype files should go, recommending docs/prototypes, in the same message as the availability table
Asks the user to confirm the inputs before proposing answers
Creates no file or folder in this turn (no scaffold.mjs run): discovery only reads
Does not write flow.json or draw anything in this turn

evals.name: proposes-documented-answers-for-approval
evals.setup: The user already chose docs/prototypes as the prototype folder.
evals.prompt: Prototype the meter pairing onboarding. The docs in docs/ and design/ are authoritative; nothing else to add.
expectations: Presents a table of proposed answers taken from the documents, each with a source citation (file and section or fact ID)
Includes at least: primary users (adults with type 2 diabetes, many over 60), units (mmol/L), max 3 meters, skip-pairing option, brand colour #0B6E4F / Inter
Distinguishes documented (A) from inferred (B) answers, e.g. offline behaviour of the readings list is documented by ARCHITECTURE.md
Asks the user to approve all or correct by ID, and does not treat proposals as decided before approval
Mentions cosmetic defaults (class E) in one line rather than asking about them
Asks, in one line under the table, which sketch style the user prefers (wireflow, click-through or both) and does not write flow.json or draw anything before approval

evals.name: surfaces-the-conflict-as-a-question
evals.setup: The user already chose docs/prototypes as the prototype folder.
evals.prompt: Prototype the meter pairing onboarding. Docs are authoritative. I approve all the proposals you make from the documents.
expectations: Asks about the conflict between PRD 'leave pairing at any time' and ADR 0003 '60 s lock after cancelling mid-handshake', quoting both
Asks what the user sees during the 20–60 s initial sync and/or the 5–15 s handshake (architecture creates a UX question)
Asks about what happens when backend registration fails after pairing (partial success)
Asks no more than four questions in the round, each with options and a recommended option first
Does not ask about border radius, spacing, icon choice or other cosmetic details

evals.name: missing-spec-asks-for-description
evals.prompt: Sketch the screens of a habit tracker app for me.
expectations: Reports that no spec, architecture or design documents were found
Asks for (or drafts from the prompt and asks to confirm) a short feature description: users, goal, main journey
Does not invent a full feature set and start building without confirmation

evals.name: drawio-mcp-missing-does-not-block
evals.setup: Run in an agent session with no draw.io MCP tools available. The user already chose docs/prototypes as the prototype folder.
evals.prompt: Prototype the meter pairing onboarding from the docs.
expectations: Notices that no open_drawio_xml tool is available in the session and runs check-drawio-mcp.mjs for this agent only
Shows the result and asks before changing the agent's configuration; does not configure it without approval
Says in one line that a newly configured server loads after a restart, and that the skill works without it
Carries on with input discovery and the proposals in the same run; does not stop or wait for the tools
Records the draw.io MCP status in docs/prototypes/notes/STATE.md

evals.name: draws-the-sketch-from-the-spec
evals.setup: Gates A and B have passed for the Android meter pairing prototype (decisions in docs/prototypes/notes/DECISIONS.md, including the 60 s lock conflict resolved as a confirm dialog); the user chose the wireflow style.
evals.prompt: Carry on.
expectations: Writes docs/prototypes/flow.json: one journey, one frame per screen state (including the empty Devices state, the Bluetooth rationale, the system permission prompt, permission denied, scanning, no meter found, pairing, the stop-pairing dialog and the paired state), and a labelled flow for every transition
Branches (the permission-denied state, the stop-pairing dialog) use "below" to hang under the screen they interrupt; flows start from a control key
Generates docs/prototypes/flow.drawio with sketch.mjs; does not hand-write draw.io XML or place shapes itself
Runs sketch.mjs --check and it passes (no arrow overlaps or crosses another or runs over a screen, every label in the clear); looks at any warnings before showing the sketch

Opens or points to the diagram (sketch.mjs --open, or the file path), gives a short text outline with S-numbers, lists decisions made on the user's behalf and assumptions, and stops for the user to lock the flow
Does not create HTML, a look/ folder, scenarios or a verification log, and does not start the design phase

evals.name: stops-at-handoff
evals.setup: The Android sketch has been shown; the design phase has not been discussed.
evals.prompt: Looks great, the flow is locked. No design pass, just give me the handoff.
expectations: Records the gate C approval in STATE.md and DECISIONS.md

Writes docs/prototypes/HANDOFF.md with the screen inventory by S-number, navigation graph, per-screen state model, Material 3 component mapping, copy, decisions with sources, open questions and the sketch as the visual reference
Says in the theme section that visual design was not done, rather than inventing one
Says plainly what was not checked: nothing was run as an app
Writes no Compose, SwiftUI, Kotlin or Swift code and stops after the handoff

evals.name: ios-target-with-android-architecture
evals.prompt: We're building the iPhone version now. Prototype the meter pairing onboarding for iOS.
expectations: Records the target platform as iOS from the user's instruction (P5), citing the prompt
Notices that ARCHITECTURE.md and ADR 0003 describe Android-specific pairing (Companion Device Manager) and asks how pairing works on iOS, rather than copying the Android behaviour
Plans the Bluetooth permission the iOS way: optional pre-prompt, one system alert with a purpose string, one denial is final with an Open Settings path
Follows references/platforms/ios/conventions.md when planning the flow (navigation bar back button, no FAB, alerts / action sheets, tab bar, modal tasks with Cancel)
Records iOS as the platform in STATE.md and, later, in flow.json ("platforms": ["ios"])
Does not write flow.json before gate A, and does not generate SwiftUI code

evals.name: one-sketch-for-both-platforms
evals.setup: Gates A and B have passed with P5 = both Android and iOS; the user chose click-through.
evals.prompt: Carry on and draw it.
expectations: Writes one flow.json with platforms [android, ios]: a single shared flow, not one per platform

Notes platform differences on the frames that have them (for example: iOS permission denial is final and offers Open Settings; Android can ask a second time; Android system back versus iOS back button or Cancel)
Generates the sketch with --style click-through: a map page plus one page per screen
sketch.mjs --check passes and the user is asked to lock the flow

evals.name: handoff-both-platforms
evals.setup: Two-platform sketch locked at gate C; the design phase was declined.
evals.prompt: Locked for both platforms, thanks. Handoff please.
expectations: HANDOFF.md has a component mapping for Android (Material 3) and for iOS (SwiftUI), marking components with no native equivalent (such as the undo toast) as custom
Lists the intended SF Symbol for each icon and each iOS permission purpose string in the copy section
Describes where navigation differs between the platforms (system back and leaving the app vs back button, edge swipe and modal Cancel)
Says what was checked (sketch.mjs --check, who locked the flow) and what was not (nothing was run as an app), and that visual design was not done
Does not generate Compose, SwiftUI, Kotlin or Swift code

evals.name: design-phase-offered-not-forced
evals.setup: Android sketch shown; no brand colour in the documents; the user has not mentioned visual design.
evals.prompt: Looks good, lock the flow.
expectations: Records gate C as passed (flow locked)
Offers the optional design phase in one line (visual direction, design system, or straight to the handoff) and does not start it without the user's choice
Did not run theme.mjs, create DESIGN.md or a style tile, or consult a design skill at any earlier phase
If the user declines, writes the handoff, saying in the theme section that visual design was not done

evals.name: design-phase-falls-back-without-python
evals.setup: Two-platform sketch locked at gate C; the user chose a visual direction; ui-ux-pro-max is not installed and Python 3 is not available on the machine.
evals.prompt: Yes, give it a visual direction. It's a medical app for people managing diabetes.
expectations: Runs design-provider.mjs --check, then tries --install; it reports that Python 3 is missing and installs nothing
Tells the user in one line that the built-in baseline provider is used instead (and how to get Python for next time), without installing Python or stopping the phase
Proposes density, expressiveness and motion in plain language with reasons from the documents (for example restrained and minimal for a medical context) and asks in one round
Writes two DESIGN.md options with the theme block filled and a rationale for each value
Runs scripts/theme.mjs --option for each option; both contrast reports pass
Runs screens.mjs so look/ exists, and gives the user the style-tile links for each option on Android and iOS, light and dark, asking them to pick (gate D1)
After the pick, applies it with theme.mjs; the flow (screens, states, navigation, approved copy) is unchanged, and the user is asked to open look/screens.html and report its summary line
Asks for approval of the look (gate D2) and records the design mode and provider in STATE.md

evals.name: design-theme-fails-contrast
evals.setup: Two-platform sketch locked at gate C; the user chose a visual direction.
evals.prompt: Use our brand yellow, #FFCC00, as the main colour.
expectations: Runs theme.mjs with brand #ffcc00; it stops because the iOS tint would be 1.3:1 and writes no theme files
Explains in plain words why yellow can't be the iOS tint for text and buttons, and offers the suggested darker tint (keeping the yellow for fills and illustrations) or ios.tint: adjust
Does not lower the contrast requirement or hand-edit the token files to get around it
The Android scheme from the same yellow passes, because Material 3 derives accessible tones from it

evals.name: design-provider-installs-and-is-used
evals.setup: Android sketch locked at gate C; Python 3 is available; ui-ux-pro-max is not installed; network access is available.
evals.prompt: Let's do a design system for the build.
expectations: Runs design-provider.mjs --install for this agent and shows the user the notice: ui-ux-pro-max v2.15.0, MIT licence, source repository, destination folder, only that one skill, how to remove it
Uses it through design-provider.mjs --run with mobile-shaped --design-system queries and dials mapped from the three choices; uses --stack jetpack-compose only for handoff notes
Maps its output into DESIGN.md (brand, accent, fonts, contrast: high if it reports a WCAG AAA constraint) and lists the web-only parts it dropped (landing pattern, hover effects, GSAP)

Writes design-system/<app>/DESIGN.md, runs theme.mjs with --export so material-theme.json and THEME-REPORT.md land next to it, and keeps the provider's raw output under sources/ rather than a competing MASTER.md
Links the design system from the handoff's theme section

evals.name: stops-at-gate-a-with-reading-guide
evals.prompt: Prototype the meter pairing onboarding. The docs in docs/ and design/ are authoritative; nothing else to add.
expectations: Creates the workspace with scaffold.mjs: docs/prototypes/README.md, flow.json (still the empty template) and notes/STATE.md, INPUTS.md, CLARIFICATIONS.md, DECISIONS.md, and no other files
Presents the A/B proposals table and ends the turn there: flow.json is not filled in and no flow.drawio exists

Ends the message with a short reading guide: how many files were created, what to review now in order (the table first, CLARIFICATIONS.md as optional detail), what is reference only (INPUTS.md, DECISIONS.md) and what is agent notes (STATE.md, flow.json)
docs/prototypes/README.md names the current stop (gate A), what the user is asked to do, and marks each file as you / reference / agent
STATE.md records the stop under Waiting on user

evals.name: hand-edited-diagram-is-not-overwritten
evals.setup: docs/prototypes/flow.drawio was generated and the user then moved frames and added a screen by hand in draw.io.
evals.prompt: I added a 'Rename meter' screen after pairing in the diagram. Also change 'Add device' to 'Pair meter'.
expectations: sketch.mjs refuses to overwrite the hand-edited diagram; the agent does not reach for --force first
Reads the user's flow.drawio and carries their change (the new Rename meter screen and its arrows) into flow.json, asking if something about it is unclear
Applies the copy change in flow.json, not in the XML
Regenerates with --force, keeping the user's version as flow.drawio.bak, and says so
Shows the new sketch and asks again for the flow to be locked

evals.name: design-phase-renders-final-look-screens
evals.setup: Android sketch locked at gate C; the user chose a visual direction and picked option A at gate D1.
evals.prompt: Go with A.
expectations: Applies the direction with theme.mjs; it writes look/tokens/android.theme.css and notes/THEME-REPORT.md and every contrast pair passes
The final-look screens come from screens.mjs and the locked flow.json: look/screens.html shows every screen state with the same S-numbers as the sketch; nothing in look/ is edited by hand
Does not change the flow: no screens, states or transitions are added or removed in flow.json
Tells the user how to open look/screens.html (serve.mjs) and what the summary line should say, and asks them to report it instead of claiming the checks passed
Stops at gate D2 for the user's approval of the look

evals.name: asks-for-the-prototype-folder-and-uses-it
evals.setup: The agent showed the availability table and asked where the prototype files should go, recommending docs/prototypes.
evals.prompt: Documents are fine. Put the files in design/prototype-pairing.
expectations: Runs scaffold.mjs with --out design/prototype-pairing and creates README.md, flow.json and the notes there, not in docs/prototypes or prototype/
Records the chosen folder in notes/STATE.md
Every later file (INPUTS.md, CLARIFICATIONS.md, flow.drawio, HANDOFF.md) is written under design/prototype-pairing
Does not ask for the folder again

evals.name: refuses-a-prototype-folder-outside-the-project
evals.setup: The agent asked where the prototype files should go, recommending docs/prototypes.
evals.prompt: Put them in ~/Desktop/prototypes.
expectations: Does not create anything outside the project
Explains that the prototype files have to stay inside this project, and asks again, offering docs/prototypes
Creates no workspace until the user names a folder inside the project

evals.name: should-not-trigger
evals.prompt: Fix the NullPointerException in DeviceRepository.kt when the meter disconnects.
expectations: Does not invoke the mobile-prototype skill
